newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to outline Euro-tax details Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Italy to outline Euro-tax details Tuesday.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi was meeting union leaders for a second day of talks on Tuesday and was expected to later unveil details of a Euro-tax designed to get Italy in shape for Europe's planned single currency.

The prime minister's office said the meeting with Italy's three main union confederations was due to resume at 0830 GMT. The talks broke up late on Monday after more than five hours and Prodi said they were "proceeding in an extremely positive way".

Italian newspapers said the Euro-tax, which is designed to raise 12.5 trillion lire ($8.3 billion) to help Italy qualify for European economic and monetary union at the start in 1999, would cost Italians between 400,000 and two million lire.

Newspapers gave conflicting figures about how much would be raised by a hike in income tax. Most put the sum at about some 8.5 trillion lire payable between May and June next year, and said it would be partly reimbursed.
Financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore said a rise in income tax would raise some 5.5 trillion lire and a further three trillion would be raised by collecting other taxes which have not yet been paid.
Italians would be given the choice of being able to reclaim about half of the tax through a rebate at a later date or to take shares in public or privatised firms, the newspapers said.
Prodi said late on Monday that precise figures would be released at a news conference at the end of Tuesday's meeting.
The meeting, called to discuss union concerns over the impact of the 1997 budget, appeared to avert the possibility of a threatened general strike.

Prodi's draft 1997 budget, which aims to slash 62.5 trillion lire off next year's public sector deficit, was passed by the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) at the weekend and moves to the Senate on Thursday.

Prodi also said that Labour Minister Tiziano Treu would call a special meeting between metalworkers threatening more strike action and their employers' federation if talks over a new contract did not reach a breakthrough in 10 days.
Metalworkers' unions have scheduled a strike for November 22, which would be their second such action in two months, after delays to renew their contracts which expired in June. ($1=1,512 lire)
